title: ready-07: extension services on the server — what heca-pro mounts its services on
summary: A public, generic way for an extension to run a service inside the heca server (daemon and standalone), with its own lifecycle, context, wakeup, client projection and action access.
description:
Requested by heca-pro (Heca-Pro P003(F001)/T013, also consumed by T014). Proposed contract: `~/projects/heca-pro-feat-13/docs/open-heca-work.md:40` ("Server service contract for T013"). heca owns the generic mounting, lifecycle, wakeup, action context and client projection; heca-pro owns its service implementation, room logic and archive. heca must stay generic: no heca-pro room or conversation types in heca.

## Current state (verified on main a5dd334d, 2026-11-14)
- The public extension entry point `heca::extension(name)` (`heca/src/entry/extension.rs:44`) offers only actions (`:80`), layers (`:87`), terminals (`:105`) and pane contributions (`pane_button`, `pane_chip`, `pane_line`). There is no server-side service.
- An extension action handler is `Fn(&mut ProviderCx, &Intent) -> Handled` (`heca/src/entry/action.rs:45`; `ProviderCx` at `heca/src/providers/mod.rs:230`). It reads the chrome store and emits intents; it cannot reach server state or a service.
- The headless server `serve()` (`heca/src/server/runtime/headless.rs:7`) builds the `ServerLoop` and calls `register_extensions` (`heca/src/server/run/mod.rs:101`), which registers only queued actions (`entry/action.rs:110`).
- Nothing server-side is publicly exported from `heca/src/lib.rs`.

## Reusable building blocks (internal today)
- Waking the owner loop from another thread and submitting work: the notification sink does exactly this (`headless.rs:14` `install_notification_sink` → `RuntimeHandle::raise` → `Event::Notification`; `heca/src/server/runtime/mod.rs:17` `Event`, `:29` `RuntimeHandle`, `:142` `dispatch`).
- Per-topic projections sent to attached clients on attach and on change: `publish_notifications` / `publish_windows` (`heca/src/server/session/publish.rs:96`, `:72`), and the script event stream `StreamEvent` / `EventFanout` (`heca/src/server/events.rs:22`, `:37`, T546).
- Identities: `heca_core::layout::SessionId` (public) and `Connection.id` (`heca/src/server/connection.rs:19`, internal; the one window identity, decision 2534270c).
- Wire vocabulary: `ClientMsg` / `ServerMsg` (`heca/src/server/wire/mod.rs:35`, `:93`).

## Behaviour to provide (from the heca-pro contract, to be agreed first)
1. A builder-style extension declaration registers a service factory before `heca::run()`. The host invokes it once per actual server (daemon and standalone), never per window, dock, session switch or snapshot.
2. Lifecycle without a window, winit or GPU; closing a client does not stop it; server shutdown stops it once, with bounded queues and visible failures.
3. A public context with the configuration/path owner and the real server/session/client identities (reuse `SessionId` and `Connection.id`; no second window identity; a request never asserts its sender).
4. Background work wakes the loop and submits bounded results without polling or blocking dispatch; service data is committed before the projection event that announces it.
5. The existing transport carries an initial extension snapshot plus versioned deltas to permitted clients; reattach or a lost/expired cursor gets a fresh snapshot; a client is never the authority.
6. Registered actions reach their owning service through public context; native UI, RPC and other commands keep the existing action/permission/result door. No second server, private dispatcher or terminal-input injection.

## Rules
AGENTS.md § 0 and Rule Zero: the API is what a plugin author types (builder on the extension, no registry lookups, ids or crate-private types in authoring). Reuse the wakeup, projection and identity mechanisms above instead of a parallel path. Work in its own worktree; the shape is agreed with heca-pro before code.

Depends on: P104 (server/client split), P099 (socket, events), P100 (sessions) — all in place.

tasks.title: Extension services on the server: mount, lifecycle, context, wakeup, client projection, action access
tasks.description:
One generic capability for heca-pro (and any extension): run a service inside the heca server. Full context, code references and the requested behaviour are in the phase P108(F012) description; the heca-pro proposal is `~/projects/heca-pro-feat-13/docs/open-heca-work.md:40`.

What exists vs what to build:
- Exists: extension entry point with actions/layers/terminals/pane contributions (`heca/src/entry/extension.rs:44`); action handlers get `ProviderCx` only (`heca/src/entry/action.rs:45`); `ServerLoop::register_extensions` registers actions only (`heca/src/server/run/mod.rs:101`); the headless entry (`heca/src/server/runtime/headless.rs:7`); internal wakeup via `RuntimeHandle` (`heca/src/server/runtime/mod.rs:29`), already used by notifications (`headless.rs:14`); per-topic client projections (`heca/src/server/session/publish.rs:72`, `:96`) and the event stream (`heca/src/server/events.rs`).
- To build: a public service declaration on the extension builder, a host-owned lifecycle per server, a public service context, a supported wakeup/submit path, a generic versioned snapshot+delta projection to clients over the existing `ClientMsg`/`ServerMsg` transport, and action access to the owning service.

Steps are the checklist. Step 1 (agree the API shape with the heca-pro agent) comes before any code; record the agreed shape as an Accepted Decision on this task.

Edge cases to cover: daemon vs standalone (one invocation per server, not per window); several servers in one process get separate service instances; client detach/reattach and session switch never restart the service; lost or expired cursor → fresh snapshot; server shutdown stops workers once; a failing factory is reported visibly and does not take the server down silently; no heca-pro types in heca.

---
**Completion summary:**
Shipped on branch feat/t553-extension-services (worktree heca-feat-553), following decision c7fb5fc3.

Authoring API, in heca/src/entry/service/:
- `ext.service(short, factory) -> ServiceRegistration<S>`, plus the trait `Service` (receive / project / stop, `SCHEMA_VERSION`).
- `registration.action(meta, handler)`, where the handler receives `&mut S` and returns `ActionResult::{Done, Refused, Later(ticket)}`.
- `registration.client(initial, apply) -> ServiceState<C>`, a reactive value on the window.
- `ServiceInbox` is bounded and Send, and a send wakes the server through the RuntimeHandle waker.
- Contexts: `StartCx`, `ServiceCx` (republish, complete), `ActionCx` (session, optional client, effective session config, later), `ProjectCx` (session, client, config, epoch, since).

Host, in heca/src/server/services/:
- Started in `ServerLoop::from_config`, so once per server, for both the daemon and standalone. Two servers in one process each start their own.
- Each pump drains the inboxes.
- Projections are computed per window (session plus connection), with per-window revisions and a server epoch. A window gets a snapshot on attach, on reattach, on `ClientMsg::ServiceResync`, and when it holds data from another server run. Updates are checked against `max_frame_bytes`.
- Wire messages: `ServerMsg::Service` and `ClientMsg::ServiceResync`.
- Deferred tickets keep the RPC reply until the service settles them; a window is told only about a refusal.
- `shutdown` calls stop until Done, delivering inbox messages in between, within `stop_timeout_ms`, then answers the callers still waiting. The daemon loop end now calls `shutdown`.
- A failing factory, message or projection is reported as a notification plus a line on stderr. Start-up reports are held for the first session.

Routing:
- Service action metadata enters the one catalog through `register_queued_actions`, as `DynamicHandler::Service`. A name already taken is refused and reported.
- A window's call goes `ClientMsg::Invoke` → session → host.
- A script's direct call goes `begin_rpc` → `rpc_service`, using the shared check `check_server_intent` extracted from `execute_server_with`.
- A script chain that ends in a service action now works too: `execute_server_with` hands its callers a `ServerStep::{Action, Service}`.

Settings: `[settings.services] inbox_capacity = 256, stop_timeout_ms = 3000` (config.default.toml, heca-config/src/settings/services.rs). `StartupQueue` gained `close` / `is_closed` / `peek`, so every server reads the service declarations.

Docs:
- docs/extending-heca.md, section "A service inside the server".
- docs/server-client-architecture.md, section "Extension services".

Verification:
- Unit tests: 5 in entry/service/tests.rs and 9 in server/run/service_tests.rs. They cover:
  - one instance per server, never restarted by detach or reattach;
  - snapshot, then delta, then reattach or resync giving a snapshot;
  - a script answered at once, deferred, or with "who asked";
  - a window's call, with a refusal shown;
  - shutdown waiting for a pending stop, and stopping once;
  - a failing factory;
  - an update over the frame limit;
  - the owner loop waking for a worker's message and stopping its services at the end;
  - a script chain ending in a service action.
- Each guarded behaviour was broken on purpose and its test went red. A guard that could not be caught was redundant, so it was removed.
- `cargo test -p heca -p heca-config`: all pass, 1220 heca lib tests.
- Clippy on toolchain 1.100.0 with a forced re-lint: clean. `cargo doc --document-private-items` for heca: clean.
- Not verified: no GUI run. A component reading `ServiceState` in the real app has not been tried; there is no GUI change.

acceptedDecisions.title: Server extension services: agreed contract with heca-pro (factory + typed service + registration-bound actions)
acceptedDecisions.decision:
Agreed on 2026-11-14 between heca (Opus) and the heca-pro agent, relayed and approved by Antonio. Shape: `ext.service(name, factory)` registers a factory run once per actual server (daemon and standalone, never per window/dock/session switch/snapshot), returning a `ServiceRegistration<S>`; actions are declared on that registration and receive `&mut S` directly (no plugin-written lookups).
1. Threads: no Send/Sync on the factory or the service — registrations are thread-local and the server loop runs on the registering thread. Only the service inbox and its messages cross threads.
2. Stop: `stop(cx) -> Done | Pending`, non-blocking, safe to call repeatedly, with a shutdown deadline from config.
3. Context: a new per-run server identity (epoch); the session's effective configuration is available to actions and projections. heca-pro's persistent archive identity stays separate and is not heca's concern.
4. Identity: only the provenance heca really has — the session and an optional `Connection.id` (absent for windowless RPC). No promise of authentication.
5. Projection: computed by the service per recipient (session + client). `None` removes that recipient's previous projection; it does not mean "no update". Payload is serializable (JSON on the wire), with service, schema_version, server_epoch, revision, base_revision (absent for snapshots), kind snapshot|delta; attach, reconnect, different epoch or a missing revision force a snapshot; size bounds; only committed data.
6. Client: the extension applies snapshots and deltas (it knows their meaning). heca owns transport, revision checking, snapshot re-requests and public reactive access from components — no manual lookups or per-dock state copies.
7. Actions: the existing action path (`ClientMsg::Invoke` → server-side dynamic actions, same catalog/permission/RPC door), returning either an immediate result or a deferred ticket the service completes after commit. A timeout or disconnect never re-runs the action nor implicitly cancels an accepted transaction.
8. Names: `<extension>.<action>`; duplicates are refused with a visible error.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: heca-pro needs a server-resident service (rooms) built on open heca. The corrected contract matches what heca really has: thread-local registration on the owner thread, ServerWaker-based wakeup, JSON wire, per-recipient projections (as per-window notifications), the existing server-side dynamic action path, local owner-only identity. It keeps heca generic and the authoring API Rule-Zero compliant.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Reuse: RuntimeHandle/Event wakeup used by the notification sink (heca/src/server/runtime/mod.rs, headless.rs:14) for the bounded service inbox; per-recipient projection like `visible_notifications_for`; `ClientMsg::Invoke` → `execute_server_dynamic` (heca/src/server/session/mod.rs:366, heca/src/actions/registry/mod.rs:188) for actions; `<extension>.<short>` naming and the existing duplicate refusal. New: server epoch; deferred correlated replies (today RPC answers are synchronous with a timeout, heca/src/server/socket/runtime.rs:89); a generic versioned extension projection message in ClientMsg/ServerMsg; a client-side public reactive accessor fed by the extension's snapshot/delta appliers; per-service inbox bounds and shutdown deadline as config keys. Still to fix exact signatures during implementation: how the service signals "republish" (e.g. after commit) so heca recomputes per-recipient projections, and the client-side accessor/applier declaration on the registration.

checklist.title: Agree the public API shape with the heca-pro agent (service declaration, context, wakeup, projection, action access); record it as an Accepted Decision

Service declaration on the extension builder + host-owned lifecycle: created once per server (daemon and standalone), unaffected by clients/session switches, stopped once on shutdown with visible failures
Public service context: configuration/path owner and real server/session/client identities (reuse SessionId and Connection.id; no second window identity; requests never assert their sender)
Wakeup and bounded result submission from background work, reusing the RuntimeHandle path the notification sink uses; data committed before its projection event

Generic extension projection: initial snapshot + versioned deltas to permitted clients over the existing ClientMsg/ServerMsg transport; fresh snapshot on reattach or lost cursor; clients never authoritative
Registered actions reach their owning service through public context, through the existing action/permission/result door (UI, RPC)
Tests (daemon + standalone, reattach, shutdown, multiple servers) and docs (docs/server-client-architecture.md + the extension authoring guide)

tasks.title: Extension services: persistent data folder and the extension's own configuration
tasks.description:
Requested by heca-pro (T013 is integrating T553 and is blocked on this), approved by Antonio on 2026-11-14. It extends the T553 contract, decision c7fb5fc3; the extension is recorded as a decision on this task.

## What exists
- `StartCx` (heca/src/entry/service/cx.rs) gives `config()`, `server_epoch()` and `inbox()`. It has no persistent path.
- The epoch changes on every start (heca/src/server/services/mod.rs `new_epoch`).
- heca's data folder is `heca_config::state_file::data_path(file)` (heca-config/src/state_file.rs), which resolves to `dirs::data_dir()/heca/<file>`.
- No server has a stable name. The socket is always `default.sock` (heca/src/server/socket/mod.rs `socket_path`).
- The server is started by `ServerLoop::from_config` (heca/src/server/bootstrap.rs) → `start_services` → `ServiceHost::start(config, wake)`. It is reached from the daemon (`heca/src/server/runtime/headless.rs` `serve`) and from standalone (`heca/src/client/local.rs` `LocalServer::new`).
- `Config` (heca-config/src/loader/mod.rs `struct Config`) has only heca's own fields. An unknown table such as `[extensions.x]` is dropped.
- Configuration layering: embedded defaults → user `config.toml` → trusted project `.heca/config.toml`.
- A session's effective config is in `SessionRuntime::config()` and reaches actions through `ActionCx::config()`.

## To build
1. **`StartCx::data_dir() -> &Path`.** The folder owned by this service on this server: `<data dir>/heca/servers/<server name>/<extension>.<service>/`.
   - The server name is `default` for the background server (`heca --server`) and `standalone` for a standalone window. It is passed into `ServerLoop::from_config` by each entry point; it is not guessed.
   - heca creates the folder owner-only (0700) before calling the factory.
   - It stays stable across restarts, unlike the epoch.
   - If the platform has no data folder, the factory gets an error reported like any factory failure; it never panics.
   - Also exposed on `ServiceCx`/`ActionCx` if cheap, so a service need not store it itself.
2. **`[extensions.<name>]` in config.**
   - `Config` keeps a generic `extensions: toml::Table` (no heca-pro fields), merged per key through the same layering.
   - `extension_config::<T: DeserializeOwned>() -> Result<T, _>` on `StartCx` reads the server config, and on `ActionCx`/`ProjectCx` reads the session's effective config.
   - The extension name comes from the service registration (`<extension>.<service>` → `<extension>`), so one extension can never read another's table.
   - A missing table deserializes from an empty table, so `#[serde(default)]` types work.
   - A config reload (`ClientMsg::Reload` → `SessionRuntime::reload_config`) refreshes what actions and projections see.
3. **Docs.** docs/extending-heca.md, section "A service inside the server": data_dir and extension_config, plus an example `[extensions.demo]` block. README/config.default.toml: document that `[extensions.<name>]` exists.

## Edge cases
- A refused or late service gets no folder.
- Two servers in one process with the same name share the folder: tests must use a temp data root, never the user's real folder (inject the root).
- Never put heca-pro names in heca.

---
**Completion summary:**
Shipped on branch feat/t554-service-data-config (worktree heca-feat-554), following decision 01c25e3c.

- **`StartCx::data_dir() -> &Path`.** Also on `ServiceCx`, and through `Deref` on `ActionCx`. It is `<data dir>/heca/servers/<server>/<extension>.<service>/`, created 0700, and stays the same across restarts.
- **Server identity** (new heca/src/server/identity/: `ServerIdentity`, `ServerKind`):
  - The background server claims `default`. A standalone server claims the lowest free `standalone-<n>` by holding an exclusive lock on `servers/<name>.lock` for its life.
  - The entry points claim it and pass it into `ServerLoop::from_config(config, identity, wake)`: runtime/headless.rs serve after the listener binds, and client/local.rs.
  - A service name that is a path is refused.
  - With no data folder, or with every slot taken, each service's start fails through the existing report path and the server still runs.
- **Shared private filesystem helper** (new heca/src/server/private_fs.rs: `private_folder`, `try_lock`). The socket runtime folder, the listener lock and the identity all use it. It refuses a symlink or a file at the target, which the review found missing in the first identity version.
- **Extension configuration.**
  - `Config.extensions: toml::Table` is merged per key through the existing layering.
  - `Config::extension::<T>(name)` reads one table. `extension_config::<T>()` on `StartCx` reads the server config; on `ActionCx` and `ProjectCx` it reads the session's effective config.
  - The extension name comes from the registration, kept in `Declared`.
  - Errors use the public `ExtensionConfigError` (extension, message, Display `[extensions.x] is not valid: …`). A missing table gives the serde defaults.
- `fs2` moved to the dependencies of every platform.
- **Docs:** docs/extending-heca.md (data_dir, extension_config, an example `[extensions.demo]`, a note on trusted-project overrides of sensitive keys); config.default.toml and README note `[extensions.<name>]`.

Verification:
- New tests:
  - identity: 6;
  - private_fs: 4;
  - service data and config: 8, in server/run/service_data_tests.rs and service_tests.rs;
  - heca-config loader: 5.
- Every guarded behaviour was broken on purpose and failed a test.
- `cargo test -p heca -p heca-config`: all pass, 1238 heca lib tests.
- Clippy on 1.100.0 with a forced re-lint: clean. Rustdoc with private items: clean.

Known, not changed: two standalone windows now have separate data folders, but they still contend for the one control socket `default.sock` (the second runs without a socket, as before).

acceptedDecisions.title: Service data folder per server + service; extension config typed from [extensions.<name>]
acceptedDecisions.decision:
Agreed on 2026-11-14 by Antonio and the heca-pro agent. This extends T553 decision c7fb5fc3.
1. `StartCx::data_dir() -> &Path` returns the folder that belongs to this server and this service, in `<data dir>/heca/servers/<server>/<extension>.<service>/`. heca creates it owner-only before the factory runs. It stays the same across restarts, unlike the epoch, and is separate from every other service's folder.
2. Server naming:
   - The background server is `default`.
   - `standalone` is only a category. Two standalone windows running at the same time must never open the same archive. Each standalone server therefore claims the lowest free slot, `standalone-1`, `standalone-2` and so on, by taking an exclusive lock on it for its whole life. A restarted standalone gets its slot back, so its folder is stable.
   - The background server takes the same lock on `default`.
3. `extension_config::<T>()` reads `[extensions.<extension>]` as a typed value and returns explicit errors: a table that does not fit `T` is an error, never a silent default. A missing table reads as an empty table.
   - On `StartCx` it reads the server's configuration.
   - On `ActionCx` and `ProjectCx` it reads the session's effective configuration, the same one `config()` returns.
   - The extension name comes from the registration, so an extension cannot read another extension's table.
4. heca carries no heca-pro fields: `[extensions.*]` is a generic table.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: heca-pro (T013) needs an archive per server that is found again after a restart. The epoch cannot do that because it changes on every start. Two concurrent standalone windows sharing one archive would corrupt it. A typed read with explicit errors catches configuration mistakes early, and reading the session's effective configuration keeps it consistent with `config()`.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes:
- Data root: `heca_config::state_file::data_path` / `dirs::data_dir()`. Tests inject a temporary root.
- Slot lock: reuse the exclusive file lock pattern of the socket listener (heca/src/server/socket/listener.rs takes a lock on default.lock). Hold the lock in the ServiceHost or ServerLoop for the server's life.
- The server name is passed explicitly by the daemon entry (`headless.rs` serve) and by standalone (`client/local.rs`) into `ServerLoop::from_config`.
- `Config` gets a generic `extensions` table merged through the existing layering.

tasks.title: Persistent session key for extension services (SessionKey)
tasks.description:
Requested by heca-pro (T013) and approved by Antonio on 2026-11-14. The contract is the accepted decision on this task.

## Problem
- A session's id is `SessionId` (heca_core::layout::SessionId, a u64) handed out per server run by `ServerLoop` (heca/src/server/run/sessions.rs `create_session`, `next_session`).
- A restarted headless server hands out ids from 1 again, so a new session C can get the old session A's id.
- An extension that keys stored data by `ActionCx::session()` / `ProjectCx::session()` (heca/src/entry/service/cx.rs) can therefore attach A's data to C.

## To build
1. **Public `SessionKey` type** (exported next to the service types in heca/src/entry/mod.rs and heca/src/lib.rs):
   - opaque, `Clone + Eq + Hash + Debug + Serialize + Deserialize`;
   - 128 random bits, from the OS random source through `getrandom`, already in Cargo.lock;
   - never a string to interpret: `Display` may print it for logs, but nothing parses it.
2. **Owned by the session.** Add it to `SessionInfo` (heca/src/server/sessions/mod.rs) or the `SessionRuntime` identity.
   - A new key when a session is created from scratch (`create_session`, and the first session made on attach).
   - The same key through rename, terminate, restart and attach/detach. It goes when the session is deleted.
   - Independent of name, folder and connection id.
   - `SessionInfo` is on the wire (ServerMsg::Sessions/Attached): decide whether the key travels to clients. Only if something needs it; otherwise keep it server-side.
3. **Exposed** as `ActionCx::session_key() -> &SessionKey` and `ProjectCx::session_key() -> &SessionKey`. `session()` stays unchanged as the id for this run. Thread the key through `services::Caller` / `Audience` (heca/src/server/services/) from the session that ran the action or is being projected.
4. **Docs:** docs/extending-heca.md "A service inside the server", explaining when to use `session()` versus `session_key()`.

## Not here
Persisting the key and restoring the same key after a server restart belong to P105(F012)/T527, recorded there as a requirement. Until T527 ships, a restarted server's sessions are new, with new keys, so stored data for an old key is simply not matched.

## Tests
- Two sessions get different keys.
- Rename, terminate and restart keep the key.
- A session created after a server restart with a reused numeric id gets a different key.
- `ActionCx` and `ProjectCx` report the key of their own session.
- The key round-trips through serde.

---
**Completion summary:**
Shipped on branch feat/t556-session-key (worktree heca-feat-556), following decision 15768fa9.

- **Public `SessionKey`** (heca/src/entry/service/session_key.rs, exported from the crate root):
  - Copy/Eq/Hash, opaque, 128 random bits from `getrandom` (0.3, already locked);
  - Display and serde use 32 hex digits, and deserializing rejects anything else;
  - no public constructor.
- **Where it lives.** The key is a field of `SessionRuntime`, made in `SessionRuntime::new`, the path every session goes through. It is kept out of `SessionInfo`, so it is not on the wire. Rename, terminate, restart and attach/detach never touch it, and Delete drops it with the session.
- **API.** `ActionCx::session_key()` and `ProjectCx::session_key()`; `session()` is unchanged.
- **Threading.** One `SessionRef { id, key }` now replaces the bare `SessionId` in `ServiceHost::invoke`/`run_step`/`Caller`, so a new path cannot forget the key. Covered paths:
  - a window's Invoke;
  - `rpc_service`;
  - `run_rpc_service`;
  - a session chain through `ServerInvocation`;
  - projections, through `Audience`.
- **Docs:** docs/extending-heca.md explains `session()` against `session_key()`, and says keys are new after a server restart until T527.

Verification:
- New tests in heca/src/server/run/service_key_tests.rs:
  - distinct keys;
  - kept through rename, terminate and restart;
  - a reused numeric id on a new server gives a new key;
  - every path reports its own session's key, across two sessions;
  - a projection gets its own session's key;
  - serde round-trip, and invalid input rejected.
- Two guarded behaviours were broken on purpose, and their tests failed.
- `cargo test -p heca`: 1245 lib tests pass, re-run by me after review. Clippy and rustdoc are clean.

Remaining, owned by T527 (C12): persist the key and restore the same key after a server restart.

acceptedDecisions.title: SessionKey: heca-owned persistent session identity for extensions
acceptedDecisions.decision:
Agreed on 2026-11-14 by Antonio and the heca-pro agent (T013).
- heca owns a persistent session identity, distinct from the run-time `SessionId`.
- It is a public `SessionKey` type: opaque and serializable, never a string to interpret.
- `cx.session_key()` on `ActionCx` and `ProjectCx` returns it. `cx.session()` is unchanged and stays this run's id.
- The key is new for a session created from scratch. It is kept through rename, terminate, restart, attach and detach, and when the same session is restored after a server restart; that restore is P105(F012)/T527.
- It goes with Delete.
- It is independent of name, folder and connection id. No identity is ever rebuilt from name or path alone, because several sessions can share a project.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: A restarted headless server hands out `SessionId`s from 1 again, so an extension keying stored data by `session()` could attach an old session's data to a new one. Several sessions can share one folder, so name and path are not identities either. An opaque type keeps extensions from parsing or building keys.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes:
- 128 random bits from `getrandom`, already in Cargo.lock.
- Owned with the session identity (SessionInfo / SessionRuntime) and threaded through `services::Caller` / `Audience` into `ActionCx` / `ProjectCx`.
- Until T527 ships, a restarted server's sessions get new keys. Run-time association is correct; recovery after a restart depends on T527.
- Heca-Pro T013 links to this decision rather than duplicating it.

tasks.title: Action policy for every request, and an external-request door for services (heca-pro T014)
tasks.description:
Requested by heca-pro (F001/P003/T014). The contract was agreed with heca-pro and approved by Antonio on 2026-11-15; it is the accepted decision on this task. Implement after P105/T527.

## What exists
- Service actions run through `ServiceHost::invoke` and `run_step` (heca/src/server/services/mod.rs).
- Script lines go through `ServerLoop::begin_rpc` / `rpc` / `rpc_service` (heca/src/server/run/).
- The shared check is `check_server_intent` (heca/src/actions/registry/server.rs): catalog, arguments, interaction policy and confirm gate.
- Chained follow-ups run through `execute_server_with` → `ServerStep`.
- A window's call goes `ClientMsg::Invoke` → session (heca/src/server/session/mod.rs).
- `ActionCx`/`ProjectCx` carry the session id, the SessionKey (T556) and the client.
- There is no authorization hook and no way for a service to submit a request on someone else's behalf.

## To build (see the decision for the exact contract)
1. **`registration.action_policy(|service, cx, request| -> Permit)`.**
   - With no policy declared, behaviour stays as today: local requests pass, external ones are refused.
   - With policies declared, every declared policy checks every request, local or external; the first deny wins.
   - It is consulted at execution time, for every catalog action: native, plugin and chained.
   - The requester is carried to chained actions.
   - Wire it once, in the shared execution path used by window, socket, helper and chain, so there is no per-handler check and no second path.
2. **`Requester::{Local { window: Option<u64> }, External { service, sender }}`**, plus `request.session() -> Option<SessionKey>` and `cx.sender()` on `ActionCx`.
3. **`cx.submit(ExternalRequest { sender, session, request_id, line }) -> Result<RequestRef, SubmitError>`.**
   - It answers at once. Errors: `QueueFull`, `UnknownSession`, `DuplicateId` (an id equal to a still-open request in this service), `Refused`.
   - The queue capacity goes in `[settings.services] request_queue_capacity` (config.default.toml + README); line length is bounded by `max_frame_bytes`.
   - It uses the same parser, catalog, confirmations and execution as RPC. A confirm-gated action is refused for an external sender.
4. **`Service::request_done(&mut self, cx, &RequestRef, RequestOutcome)`.**
   - `RequestRef` holds service, sender, session and request_id. `RequestOutcome` is `Done`, `Refused`, `Failed` or `Unknown`.
   - For a chain, `Done` comes only after every action and every deferred ticket finishes. A refusal or error mid-chain is `Failed`, and earlier actions are not undone.
   - At shutdown: a request never started is `Refused`; one started but unfinished is `Unknown`.
   - Nothing is persisted or re-executed after a restart.
5. **Docs:** docs/extending-heca.md, covering the security limit exactly as agreed and that `Sender::new` authenticates no one.

## Tests (heca's share)
- The same policy applies for window, socket and helper.
- The requester propagates, and a chain never escalates.
- A revocation applies to queued requests.
- The session is explicit: unknown → refused, never substituted.
- Queue full; a duplicate open id.
- A deferred result arrives correlated; `Unknown`/`Refused` at shutdown; no re-execution.
- No policy → local passes and external is refused.
- A confirm-gated action is refused for an external sender.

heca-pro owns: member→role mapping, RolePermissions, the message format, room replies, persistent dedup, and the check that the sender comes from trusted integration metadata.

---
**Completion summary:**
Merged in PR #314. CI was green on the PR (run 43718695041) and on main after the merge (run 43719605405).

Following decision 0be89c38 with its 2026-11-15 clarifications:
- **One check.** `ServiceHost::authorize` (server/services/permit.rs), reached from `execute_server_with` (calls and chain follow-ups) and from the server's receipt of window messages (session `Act`/`Invoke`, and session-management `Act` in the server loop). `check_server_intent` is private. Reads are covered.
- **Requester.** Local window or script, or external sender with its service, propagated down chains.
- **`cx.submit`.** It answers at once: QueueFull, UnknownSession, DuplicateId or Refused. It goes through the same parser, catalog and execution, never reaches a window, and refuses queries.
- **Completion.** `Service::request_done` with Done, Refused, Failed or Unknown; shutdown gives Refused or Unknown; nothing is persisted or re-run.
- **Declared confirmations.** An action that declares a confirmation is always refused for an external sender, whatever the `[confirm]` config; local behaviour is unchanged.
- **Setting:** `[settings.services] request_queue_capacity = 64`.
- **Docs:** extending-heca.md with the exact security limit; server-client-architecture.md.
- **Tests:** 15 in server/run/policy_tests.rs. Four guarded behaviours were broken on purpose, and each time a test failed. 1307 heca lib tests pass.

Outside the policy by agreement:
- window-only view actions;
- script queries `list-actions` and `describe-action` for the local user.

Open: heca-pro asks that `kill-server` become a catalog action under the same policy. That is a contract extension to agree in a new task.

acceptedDecisions.title: Contract: action policy for every request and the external-request door (agreed with heca-pro T014)
acceptedDecisions.decision:
Agreed with heca-pro (F001/P003/T014) and approved by Antonio on 2026-11-15. Clarified the same day, after implementation review: see points 1 and 3.

1. **Policy.** `registration.action_policy(|service, cx, request| -> Permit /* Allow | Deny(reason) */)`.
   - With no policy declared, behaviour stays as today: local requests pass, external requests are refused.
   - With policies declared, every declared policy checks every request, local or external, and the first deny wins. An external request is also refused when its originating service has no policy.
   - **Scope (clarified):** the policy covers every action the server executes, including reads such as listing sessions, not only actions that change shared state. It covers native, plugin, service and chained actions, and is consulted at execution time, so a revocation applies to queued requests.
   - **Window-only view actions** (focus, scroll, menus and the like, which run inside a window and never reach the server) are outside the policy. An external sender can never run them, and never gets a privileged forward to a window. Any server action a chain produces is still checked with the original requester.
   - The requester propagates to chained actions, so a chain never escalates.
   - A local refusal shows as a notification in the window or as `error: …` for scripts.
   - heca keeps no escape hatch. The default full-access local role is heca-pro's responsibility (their decision 63).
2. **Requester and session.**
   - `enum Requester { Local { window: Option<u64> }, External { service, sender } }`, where an external requester keeps its originating service.
   - The request exposes `requester()`, `action()`, `args()`, `session() -> Option<SessionKey>` and `parent() -> Option<&str>`.
   - A local request may have no session (global actions such as listing or creating sessions).
   - `cx.sender()` on `ActionCx`.
3. **External request door.** `cx.submit(ExternalRequest { sender, session, request_id, line }) -> Result<RequestRef, SubmitError>`, answering at once.
   - `SubmitError` is `QueueFull`, `UnknownSession`, `DuplicateId` or `Refused(reason)`.
   - The session is mandatory and verified; heca never invents a session or substitutes the last one.
   - The queue capacity is configurable in `[settings.services]`; line length is bounded by `max_frame_bytes`.
   - It uses the same parser, catalog, confirmations and execution as RPC, with no second path.
   - **Confirmation (clarified):** an action that declares a confirmation (`ActionMeta.confirm` present) is always refused for an external sender, whatever the user's local confirmation setting, including when the user has turned that confirmation off. The rule keys on a declared confirmation, never on a "danger" colour or style. For local requests, the policy and the user's confirmation settings apply as before. The same rule holds inside chains, without losing the external identity.
4. **Completion.** `Service::request_done(&mut self, cx, &RequestRef, RequestOutcome)`.
   - `RequestRef` holds service, sender, session (SessionKey) and request_id.
   - `RequestOutcome` is one of:
     - `Done(Option<String>)`: done, only after every action and deferred ticket in the chain finishes;
     - `Refused(reason)`: refused before anything ran;
     - `Failed(reason)`: ended with an error, possibly after partial effects, including a refusal mid-chain; earlier actions are not undone;
     - `Unknown`: the conclusion cannot be known.
5. **Duplicates and restart.**
   - heca refuses a request_id equal to a still-open request in the same service. It does not remember completed ids; persistent dedup is heca-pro's job, with its archive.
   - The queue is not persisted. At shutdown, a request never started is `Refused("server stopped, not executed")` and a request started but unfinished is `Unknown`.
   - After a restart nothing is re-executed; `Unknown` never becomes a new execution.
6. **Security limit, stated exactly.** Any process of the same user can open the socket directly. Without effective isolation, such as a different OS user, permissions limit requests received through cooperating integrations, not a hostile local process. Nothing more is promised. `Sender::new(...)` authenticates no one.
7. **Who verifies what.**
   - heca tests: the common policy across window, socket and helper; requester propagation; revocation; chains; the explicit session; deferred results; queue full; duplicates; the shutdown outcomes; a declared confirmation refused for an external sender even with that confirmation turned off, directly and in a chain.
   - heca-pro verifies that the sender comes from trusted integration metadata, never from message content, and owns member→role mapping, RolePermissions, the message format and room replies.
   - heca adds no Pro types.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: heca-pro needs room members to drive heca actions under roles, without duplicating heca's action path or trusting message content. A policy wired into the one execution path covers every surface and every chained action. Explicit outcomes, duplicates and restart behaviour remove guesswork on both sides. The security limit is stated so no isolation is promised that the local socket cannot give.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes:
- Wire the policy in the shared path (`check_server_intent` / `execute_server_with` / `ServiceHost::invoke`), never per handler.
- The requester travels with `SessionRef`/`Caller` and with `ServerStep` follow-ups.
- Heca-Pro T014 links to this decision and does not duplicate it.
- Implement after P105/T527.

EXTENSION, agreed with heca-pro and approved by Antonio on 2026-11-15, implemented in P108(F012)/T559:
8. **Stopping the server is the catalog action `kill_server`.**
   - It is the one path for the CLI (`heca --kill-server`), the palette and any key binding. It has no default key and no new confirmation.
   - The old raw socket line `kill-server` goes away, and so does every separate check for it. Scripts use `heca rpc kill_server`, documented as replacing `heca rpc kill-server`.
   - The action policy can forbid it for the local user. With no policy it behaves as before.
   - External senders are always refused, also inside chains. Like session management, it is a server action that a submitted request gets as not runnable, whatever the policy says.
   - Script queries `list-actions` and `describe-action` stay outside the policy for the local user and unreachable for senders.
   - Nothing claims to stop the user ending the process from the operating system.

Requester (Local{window} | External{service, sender}), request.session(): Option<SessionKey>, cx.sender() on ActionCx

cx.submit(ExternalRequest) answering at once (QueueFull/UnknownSession/DuplicateId/Refused); configurable request_queue_capacity; same parser/catalog/confirm/execution as RPC; confirm-gated refused for external

Service::request_done(RequestRef, RequestOutcome Done/Refused/Failed/Unknown): chain Done only after all actions and tickets; mid-chain error = Failed; shutdown Refused/Unknown; nothing persisted or re-executed
Tests (heca's share per the decision) and docs incl. the agreed security limit

tasks.title: kill_server as a catalog action under the action policy (T557 extension)
tasks.description:
This implements point 8 of decision 0be89c38 on P108(F012)/T557, extended with heca-pro on 2026-11-15 and approved by Antonio.

## What exists
- Stopping the server is a raw socket line, `KILL_SERVER = "kill-server"` in heca/src/server/run/mod.rs.
- `ServerLoop::begin_rpc` recognises it before any check and calls `shutdown()`. The action policy (`ServiceHost::authorize`, T557) never sees it.
- `heca --kill-server` (heca/src/app/cli/) sends that line; `heca rpc kill-server` works the same way.
- heca-pro's probe calls the old line in four places and will update when it adopts this revision.

## To build
1. **`kill_server` in the catalog.** A built-in descriptor (label, description, icon, category System, `args: &[]`), owned by the server loop like the session-management actions, so it runs in `ServerLoop` and is reachable from the palette and RPC.
   - No default key in keybindings.default.toml.
   - No new confirmation.
   - Classify its policy in `action_policy()`, and its side.
2. **One path.** `heca --kill-server` sends the `kill_server` action. The `KILL_SERVER` raw-line special case and its constant are removed, along with any separate check. A window running `kill_server` from the palette stops the server through the same path.
3. **Policy.** It goes through `ServiceHost::authorize` for local requests, so a restricted local role can forbid it. With no policy it behaves as before.
4. **External senders are always refused,** also inside chains: a submitted request gets it as not runnable (as with `create_session`), whatever the policy says.
5. **Docs.**
   - docs/server-client-architecture.md: the kill-server mentions, and that `heca rpc kill_server` replaces `heca rpc kill-server`.
   - README: CLI and RPC sections.
   - docs/extending-heca.md: the policy section.

## Tests
- `heca --kill-server` still stops the server; the real-binary test in heca/tests/server_process.rs is updated.
- A policy that denies `kill_server` for the local user stops both the CLI and the palette path, and the server stays up.
- With no policy it works.
- An external submit of `kill_server`, directly and in a chain, is refused as not runnable even when the policy allows it.
- The old `kill-server` line is now an unknown command.

---
**Completion summary:**
Shipped in PR #315 (branch feat/t559-kill-server-action). CI run 43746220942 is green on macOS, Linux and Windows.

- **`kill_server` is a catalog action** (`WmAction::KillServer`): side Server, Global, `args: &[]`, no default key, no confirmation. The server loop owns it like the session actions (`sessions::owns`), and it runs through `ServerLoop::stop()`.
- **One path.** `heca --kill-server` sends `kill_server`, the same as `heca rpc kill_server`; the palette sends it as a window `Act`. The `KILL_SERVER` raw line and its special case are removed, and `heca rpc kill-server` is now an unknown command (documented in README, server-client-architecture.md and extending-heca.md).
- **Policy.** It goes through `ServiceHost::authorize`, so a policy can forbid it for a script or a window, and the server stays up. An external submit is always not runnable, also in chains.
- **Fixed on the way:**
  - a window was never told when the server loop refused one of its own actions; `report_refusal` now raises the notification;
  - a chain follow-up that could not run was reported under the chain's name; it now names the follow-up.
- **Two intermittent tests fixed:**
  - the socket listener test: a concurrently spawned child could inherit the listening socket, so the stale-socket check moved to its own process, heca/tests/stale_socket.rs;
  - heca-core's agent-reporting test compared the foreground process group, which moves when the shell starts the job; it now compares the pty child pid (`child_pid`, used only by the unix test).
- **Tests:** a policy forbids kill_server for a script and a window; a window stops the server with no policy; a sender can never stop it; the old line is unknown; the real-binary `--kill-server` test. Breaking the window path's check on purpose made a test fail.

- The first commit was made by a command chain that went ahead despite a failing test run (the flaky socket test).
- The Windows CI failed once on a test helper used only on unix, because Windows clippy was not run locally for heca-core before that push.
